q: Is a company bus or contracted staff transport Scope 1 or Scope 3 Category 7?
title: Staff bus: Scope 1 or Category 7?
short: It depends on who operates the bus. A bus you own, or lease and run with your own drivers and fuel, is Scope 1. A bus run by a transport contractor who supplies vehicle, driver and fuel is Scope 3; Category 7, employee commuting, is the closer fit, though some companies use Category 1. Disclose your choice.

sections.h: Four common set-ups and where each goes
ul: Company-owned bus, company driver, company buys diesel: Scope 1.
Bus on lease, company driver and fuel: Scope 1 under the operational control approach most companies use. Under financial control, an operating lease moves it to Scope 3 Category 8.

Company-owned bus, but a contractor drives it and buys the fuel: decided by who has operational control under the contract. Read the contract, record the answer, and treat every such bus the same way.
Contractor's bus, driver and fuel, paid per month or per trip: Scope 3.

sections.h: Category 7 or Category 1 for a contracted bus
p: The GHG Protocol Scope 3 guidance describes Category 7 as transporting employees between their homes and worksites in vehicles the company does not own or operate. A contracted factory bus fits that wording. Category 1, purchased services, is also defended because the service arrives on an invoice. Either is acceptable if disclosed and applied every year; the error to avoid is counting the same trips in both.

ol: Best: fuel used. For your own buses this is the diesel slips; for a contractor, ask for litres bought for your routes.
Next: distance. Route km per day x days run x the bus's km per litre gives litres; then multiply by the fuel factor.
Last resort: spend. Monthly charges x a spend-based factor, labelled an estimate.

sections.h: Keep the rest of commuting separate
p: Staff who come on their own scooters or by public transport are also Category 7 but need a commuting survey. Trips to clients, airports or other plants are Category 6, business travel, even if the same bus does them.

example.title: Worked example: two contracted buses
lines: Route: 60 km a day per bus, 2 buses, 300 days a year = 36,000 km
Contractor's figure: 4 km per litre, so 36,000 divided by 4 = 9,000 litres of diesel
Emissions: 9,000 x 2.68 kg CO2 per litre (IPCC 2006 default) = 24,120 kg, about 24.1 t CO2
Reported in Scope 3 Category 7; if the buses were yours, the same 24.1 t would be Scope 1
example.note: The km per litre is the contractor's number; ask for the fuel log to confirm it.

senseible: Senseible reads diesel slips for buses you run as Scope 1 fuel, and keeps contractor invoices in the Scope 3 supplier evidence trail with the document attached. It does not convert route kilometres into fuel; you supply that calculation.

sources.label: GHG Protocol Corporate Accounting and Reporting Standard, revised edition (2004), Chapter 4 and Appendix F on leased assets
GHG Protocol Technical Guidance for Calculating Scope 3 Emissions (2013), Category 7

reviewNote: Classifying contracted buses is a judgement under current guidance; check whether the GHG Protocol revision clarifies it.
